In a star-connected system, the line voltage \( V_L \) is \( \sqrt{3} \) times the phase voltage \( V_{ph} \), and the line current \( I_L \) equals the phase current \( I_{ph} \).  
For a balanced three-phase system, power is given by:  

\[
P_{\text{star}} = \sqrt{3} \, V_L \, I_L \, \cos\phi
\]

In star connection:  
\[
V_L = \sqrt{3} \, V_{ph}, \quad I_L = I_{ph}
\]
So:
\[
P_{\text{star}} = \sqrt{3} \times (\sqrt{3} \, V_{ph}) \times I_{ph} \times \cos\phi
\]
\[
P_{\text{star}} = 3 \, V_{ph} \, I_{ph} \, \cos\phi
\]

In delta connection:  
\[
V_L = V_{ph}, \quad I_L = \sqrt{3} \, I_{ph}
\]
So:
\[
P_{\text{delta}} = \sqrt{3} \, V_L \, I_L \, \cos\phi
\]
\[
P_{\text{delta}} = \sqrt{3} \times V_{ph} \times (\sqrt{3} \, I_{ph}) \times \cos\phi
\]
\[
P_{\text{delta}} = 3 \, V_{ph} \, I_{ph} \, \cos\phi
\]

Thus \( P_{\text{delta}} = P_{\text{star}} \) for the same line voltages and line currents — but the question says "equivalent" system, meaning the same impedances per phase.  

If the same impedance \( Z \) is connected in delta instead of star, the voltage across each phase in delta is \( \sqrt{3} \) times that in star, so phase current becomes \( \sqrt{3} \) times, and power in delta becomes 3 times the star power.  

So if \( P \) is star power, equivalent delta power = \( 3P \).  

Final answer: (B)
